voucher_rent_ceiling.what_this_is: the range a PHA's voucher payment standard can be set to (90-110% of the metro/county FMR). It is a ceiling on gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities), not a promised rent: the PHA also caps rent at local comparable unassisted rents (rent reasonableness) and subtracts tenant-paid utilities. The voucher pays for the smaller of the family's voucher size and the unit's bedrooms, so extra bedrooms earn nothing.
voucher_rent_ceiling.policy_2026: HUD's 2026 Budget Management Letter pushes PHAs to cut payment standards toward the lower end of the range and to end exception payment standards; plan on the low figure.
voucher_rent_ceiling.year_note: HUD FMR/SAFMR values as stored in meta.rent (HUD eGIS layer vintage). FY2027 values took effect 2026-10-01 and may differ: confirm at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html
voucher_rent_ceiling.basis: FMR 4BR $3768 (Nassau-Suffolk, NY HUD Metro FMR Area) x 0.90 / 1.10

assistance.occupancy_by_bedrooms: up to 8 persons at 2 per bedroom (typical PHA subsidy standard)

checklist.why: 4 bedroom(s) (estimated from LiDAR footprint & stories). PHAs size vouchers at about 2 persons per bedroom; a bedroom must be a sleeping room with a window (HQS) and usually an openable egress window and a door. Extra bedrooms beyond the voucher size earn no extra subsidy. footprint 142 m2 x 2 stories (LiDAR height estimate) x 0.8 = ~227 m2 living area; conservative, capped at 4.

Gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities) must be at or below the PHA payment standard, about $3,391-$4,145/month here for 4BR, and no higher than comparable unassisted rents. We do not estimate a rent for this house. Context only: at the low ceiling, 12 months of gross rent = 6.4% of the $638,000 estimated value (ACS ACS 5-year 2020-2024 tract median value x FHFA ZIP 11756 HPI 2024->2025).
year built unknown; if before 1978 and a child under 6 will live there the Lead-Safe Housing Rule applies

NSPIRE: smoke alarm on every level, inside each bedroom and within 21 ft of each bedroom door; carbon-monoxide alarms where there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. Not visible in any dataset.
a permanently installed, working heat source (no unvented space heaters) is required in HUD-designated climate zones; also hot and cold running water. Not visible in our data.

safe path from the unit door to the street; living room and each sleeping room need a window (HQS), and most PHAs want bedroom windows that open for escape; upper-floor bedrooms: check window size and guardrails on drops of 30 in or more.
FEMA zone X (area of minimal flood hazard): outside the Special Flood Hazard Area
no warning signs in the exterior data we have (roof surface spread 12 cm), but no city code-case data for this house; interior condition unknown

bah_benchmark.note: BAH is paid to the service member, not the landlord: a rent benchmark for military tenants, not a guarantee. E-5 with dependents is the common benchmark.

voucher_rent_ceiling.what_this_is: the range a PHA's voucher payment standard can be set to (90-110% of the metro/county FMR). It is a ceiling on gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities), not a promised rent: the PHA also caps rent at local comparable unassisted rents (rent reasonableness) and subtracts tenant-paid utilities. The voucher pays for the smaller of the family's voucher size and the unit's bedrooms, so extra bedrooms earn nothing.
voucher_rent_ceiling.policy_2026: HUD's 2026 Budget Management Letter pushes PHAs to cut payment standards toward the lower end of the range and to end exception payment standards; plan on the low figure.
voucher_rent_ceiling.year_note: HUD FMR/SAFMR values as stored in meta.rent (HUD eGIS layer vintage). FY2027 values took effect 2026-10-01 and may differ: confirm at https://www.huduser.gov/portal/datasets/fmr.html
voucher_rent_ceiling.basis: FMR 3BR $3563 (Nassau-Suffolk, NY HUD Metro FMR Area) x 0.90 / 1.10

assistance.occupancy_by_bedrooms: up to 6 persons at 2 per bedroom (typical PHA subsidy standard)

checklist.why: 3 bedroom(s) (estimated from LiDAR footprint & stories). PHAs size vouchers at about 2 persons per bedroom; a bedroom must be a sleeping room with a window (HQS) and usually an openable egress window and a door. Extra bedrooms beyond the voucher size earn no extra subsidy. footprint 134 m2 x 1 stories (LiDAR height estimate) x 0.8 = ~107 m2 living area; conservative, capped at 4.

Gross rent (rent + tenant-paid utilities) must be at or below the PHA payment standard, about $3,207-$3,919/month here for 3BR, and no higher than comparable unassisted rents. We do not estimate a rent for this house. Context only: at the low ceiling, 12 months of gross rent = 6.0% of the $638,000 estimated value (ACS ACS 5-year 2020-2024 tract median value x FHFA ZIP 11756 HPI 2024->2025).
year built unknown; if before 1978 and a child under 6 will live there the Lead-Safe Housing Rule applies

NSPIRE: smoke alarm on every level, inside each bedroom and within 21 ft of each bedroom door; carbon-monoxide alarms where there are fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. Not visible in any dataset.
a permanently installed, working heat source (no unvented space heaters) is required in HUD-designated climate zones; also hot and cold running water. Not visible in our data.
safe path from the unit door to the street; living room and each sleeping room need a window (HQS), and most PHAs want bedroom windows that open for escape.
FEMA zone X (area of minimal flood hazard): outside the Special Flood Hazard Area
no warning signs in the exterior data we have (roof surface spread 15.1 cm), but no city code-case data for this house; interior condition unknown

bah_benchmark.note: BAH is paid to the service member, not the landlord: a rent benchmark for military tenants, not a guarantee. E-5 with dependents is the common benchmark.
